Neha / team — quick tech note after a run through infra: 

Summary (high level):
- Primary processing for the pilot lives in us-central GCP. No UK region processing planned today.
- Edge telemetry is routed through our CDN partner (EdgeHalo) which retains short-term logs in eu-west-1 for performance; those logs are pseudonymized for at-rest storage but some connection metadata (source IP truncation) is transiently available for 24 hours.
- Subprocessors: Core inference (Redwood runtime), CDN (EdgeHalo), observability (LogSight), KMS (CloudKMS), and backup provider (ColdStore). I'll export the CSV and include short control statements for each.

Blockers / flags: 
- If Zeno requires all processing to be demonstrably within UK borders, we need to discuss onshore cache fallback (we have a design but capacity lead time is 6-8 weeks).
- Edge log retention: for strict UK residencies we'll need to change the CDN retention TTL and provide a pseudonymization attestation.

Next steps: 
- I will drop the subprocessors CSV into the Drive folder and attach the short control statements (expected by EOD local time).

-Kim

Thanks Kim — and Neha. A few legal sequencing suggestions based on Zeno's ask and our standard DPA workflow: 

Proposed order to send (minimal friction path):
1) Subprocessor CSV + control statements (in parallel with)
2) SCCs package (redacted copy + statement of applicability)
3) KMS/HSM attestation and encryption-in-transit proofs
4) UK Addendum: draft for signature only if Zeno confirms UK-data processing; otherwise send as "for reference"
5) Post-signature: notarized subprocessor attestations and any third-party SOC2 extracts

Redlines / exceptions to watch for: 
- Zeno might insist on a signed UK Addendum before starting pilot if their compliance team is conservative — anticipate that ask and decide if we can compress the timeline
- If they request proof of onshore cache fallback prior to signature, escalate to Product for an exception (cost + schedule implications).

I'll prepare a short email bundle and suggested cover note for Zeno privacy legal.

-Marissa
Senior Counsel, Privacy | Redwood Inference
